changes_made.explanation: Removed 'WikiSQL' as it's only mentioned briefly as background, not used in evaluation. Normalized model names and removed redundant/vague model descriptions. Text-to-SQL falls under Code Generation as it generates executable code.

Normalized metric names to standard forms (title case). Combined variant names under base forms. 'Test Suite Accuracy' is mentioned as being equivalent to Execution Accuracy in this context, so removed as redundant.
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this paper. The paper mentions GPT-4 as a generation model (DIN-SQL uses GPT-4), but not as an evaluator/judge.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated redundant guideline descriptions into clear, concise points. Normalized criteria to focus on core evaluation dimensions mentioned throughout the paper: correctness and semantic equivalence of SQL queries with natural language questions.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on evaluating Text-to-SQL models and benchmarks, which is a form of code generation (SQL query generation). The extraction was generally accurate but contained some redundancy and minor inconsistencies. The paper primarily uses human evaluation with SQL experts to assess query correctness, with automatic metrics (exact match and execution accuracy) serving as baseline comparisons that are shown to be unreliable.
